title: UNIONS v2, four tomographic bins (blinded data)
summary: The four tomographic bins and n(z) of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468, measured blinded. The B-mode data vectors come first, for all ten bin pairs in three estimators, each with its errors.
banner: Blinded (blind: unions): E-mode data vectors are concealed; do not interpret cosmology
provenance: ShapePipe v2.0.0 calibrated sample, on all 22,901 run-1 tiles; 191.0M galaxies, 5,223 deg²; tomographic footprint (tiles with z-band photometry) 19,035 tiles, 4,582 deg²
recalibrated DR6 BPZ+SOM four-bin n(z) and bins of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468, on a dz = 0.05 grid; validation and null tests only; ⟨z⟩ = 0.283, 0.451, 0.618, 0.923

figures.caption: Pure-mode B-mode correlation functions θξ₊ᴮ (circles) and θξ₋ᴮ (squares) for each pair of tomographic bins, with errors from the analytic covariance. Shaded scales lie outside the 12–83′ range of the test.
figures.alt: Pure-mode B-mode correlation functions θξ₊ᴮ (circles) and θξ₋ᴮ (squares) for each pair of tomographic bins, with errors from the analytic covariance. Shaded scales lie outside the 12–83′ range of the test.

figures.caption: COSEBIs B modes Bₙ (n ≤ 20, 12–83′) for each pair of tomographic bins, in units of their own standard deviation, over bands at ±1σ and ±2σ. The modes are correlated, so single points say little.
figures.alt: COSEBIs B modes Bₙ (n ≤ 20, 12–83′) for each pair of tomographic bins, in units of their own standard deviation, over bands at ±1σ and ±2σ. The modes are correlated, so single points say little.

figures.caption: Pseudo-Cℓ BB (filled circles) and EB (open diamonds) for each pair of tomographic bins, in units of their own standard deviation from a Gaussian NaMaster covariance, over bands at ±1σ and ±2σ. The ℓ axis is linear in √ℓ, on which the 32 bandpowers are evenly spaced; BB and EB are offset slightly in ℓ to keep them apart.
figures.alt: Pseudo-Cℓ BB (filled circles) and EB (open diamonds) for each pair of tomographic bins, in units of their own standard deviation from a Gaussian NaMaster covariance, over bands at ±1σ and ±2σ. The ℓ axis is linear in √ℓ, on which the 32 bandpowers are evenly spaced; BB and EB are offset slightly in ℓ to keep them apart.

figures.caption: Blinded shear correlation functions θξ₊ (filled) and θξ₋ (open) for each pair of tomographic bins, with errors from the analytic covariance. The blinding shifts these data by an unknown cosmology, so they are shown alone, without a prediction to compare against.
figures.alt: Blinded shear correlation functions θξ₊ (filled) and θξ₋ (open) for each pair of tomographic bins, with errors from the analytic covariance. The blinding shifts these data by an unknown cosmology, so they are shown alone, without a prediction to compare against.

figures.caption: Blinded pseudo-Cℓ EE power spectra ℓCℓ for each pair of tomographic bins, on one y range and an axis linear in √ℓ, with errors from the Gaussian NaMaster covariance; shown alone for the same reason.
figures.alt: Blinded pseudo-Cℓ EE power spectra ℓCℓ for each pair of tomographic bins, on one y range and an axis linear in √ℓ, with errors from the Gaussian NaMaster covariance; shown alone for the same reason.

figures.caption: ρ statistics of the PSF stars, which measure the PSF model residuals; all four bins share them.
figures.alt: ρ statistics of the PSF stars, which measure the PSF model residuals; all four bins share them.

figures.caption: Correlations between galaxy shapes and PSF quantities for each tomographic bin (one row per bin): τ₀, and τ₂ and τ₅ multiplied by θ, with each bin's fitted leakage model as a line.
figures.alt: Correlations between galaxy shapes and PSF quantities for each tomographic bin (one row per bin): τ₀, and τ₂ and τ₅ multiplied by θ, with each bin's fitted leakage model as a line.

figures.caption: PSF-leakage coefficients α, β and η per bin, from a fit of the τ statistics to the ρ templates with ρ held fixed. The τ estimator biases α low by about 25% on a simulation with known leakage (CosmoStat/shear_psf_leakage#58), so read these α as lower limits.
figures.alt: PSF-leakage coefficients α, β and η per bin, from a fit of the τ statistics to the ρ templates with ρ held fixed. The τ estimator biases α low by about 25% on a simulation with known leakage (CosmoStat/shear_psf_leakage#58), so read these α as lower limits.

figures.caption: The four-bin redshift distributions of this run: recalibrated DR6 BPZ+SOM four-bin n(z) and bins of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468, on a dz = 0.05 grid; validation and null tests only.

figures.caption: Analytic (OneCovariance) ξ± variance divided by the data's 100-patch jackknife variance, per bin pair (auto-correlations coloured, cross-correlations grey); the band is the jackknife's own ±14% scatter. The median ratio is 0.98 below 10′ (required within 15% of 1) and 1.03 at 12–83′.
